svg.title: ACM: how the model sees its own action
svg.text: The Butterfly Model (ACM) · how the model sees its own action
Action–Worlds Consequence prediction Model, built on the Meaning Language Model. 1 actor, 1 action = consequences in cascade. Generated from a real run - nothing hand-placed.
impact spreads world by world, by proximity
atomic and chemical laws · nothing predicted in this run
physical laws: force, motion, gravity, energy
laws of vibration and signals · nothing predicted in this run
digital system laws · nothing predicted in this run
★ the action happens here: 🏛️ society & economy (the WHERE of the phrase)
instead of a new one being
desired outcome: pay my debt → ENABLED ➕
red dummy = the origin actor · red vector = its action (dashed: reaches that actor only through its consequences) · blue dummies = the other actors · blue vectors = their reactions
A reaction is the consequence for that actor's goal, computed by the engine; what they do next is not predicted here.

→ proximity: the impact spreads outward world by world, and a consequence can also flow back · ∿ synchronicity: worlds change together, down to the quantum level (correlation, not cause) · both concepts, not yet modelled
World placement: the rule engine says how far each consequence reaches, not which world it is in; the world shown is an explicit mapping for this picture, and empty worlds say so.
every node of every action graph is stored as a vector
83 dims: kind | role | entity type | circle | lemma hash | certainty · polarity · tense
cosine similarity of action nodes across stored graphs
John sold his car to Sarah.
The engineer deleted the database in production.
vectors are structural, not semantic: two nodes are close when they play the same part
in similar actions. A learned embedder can replace the hashing one behind the same interface.
scenario · context: Mark wants to buy my car. Sarah needs a car. · action: I will sell my car to Sarah in Paris tomorrow to pay my debt.
